A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MF-LAL study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original compound-generation and ABFE simulation results for BRD4(2) and c-MET, architecture ablations, oracle validation and active-learning analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated baselines and quantitative summaries of generated-compound quality.

M1.justification: The latent hierarchy, GP surrogates, losses and generation procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 replaces q_phi(x) with z_k in the uncertainty check, aligning the pseudocode with the rule already stated in v2 Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BRD4(2) and c-MET generation tasks, ZINC250k initialization, BindingDB data and DUD-E oracle-validation setting. No dataset, target, domain or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: v3 adds RGA and TAGMol, both labeled 'only docking', to the evaluated comparisons for both targets in Table 1. All previously evaluated comparator configurations remain; this is a limited extension of the existing baseline suite.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 extends evaluation with filtering acceptance rates and aggregate QED, SAscore and diversity measurements. Appendix B.3 explicitly restricts top-three statistical comparisons to methods with 40 compounds. The seven-day budget, initialization, filtering thresholds and previously reported 15-plus-25 sampling design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds diagnostics showing how many generated compounds pass filtering and their quality afterward. The existing ablation questions and variant results remain, although the full-model reference row is revised. Appendix C's oracle-output and reconstruction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies that mean comparisons use 40 compounds where available and 15 otherwise, while top-three comparisons involve only methods with 40 compounds. Student's t-tests, binomial tests and mean±SD reporting are retained; no additional seed or repeated-training-run analysis is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds RGA mean ABFE scores of -3.1/-2.1 and TAGMol scores of -1.9/-3.5 kcal/mol for BRD4(2)/c-MET. The 15-compound MF-LAL ablation row changes from means -6.3/-7.1 and 4/3 active scaffolds to -6.2/-6.7 and 6/4, with revised top-three scores. Separate 15-compound Pocket2Mol and MF-AL-PPO results are also supplied. The original 40-compound results remain in v3 Table 2. Section 4.3 adds 55%/68% filtering acceptance and post-filter quality summaries.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup and Equations 1–4, including the training objective, Gaussian likelihood expression and latent diversity term in Appendix A, are retained. No substantive theoretical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an integrated multi-fidelity generative framework, a novel query-generation technique and approximately 50% better mean binding-free-energy scores on two targets. Abstract and contribution-list edits preserve these claims' scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 gives more specific scientific justification for the existing activity thresholds through descriptions of the cited BRD4(2) and c-MET studies. It also explicitly describes the diversity finding as mean pairwise similarity. The principal mechanism interpretations and Section 5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an MF-LAL code-access link, RGA and TAGMol code references, and TAGMol's single-objective guidance configuration. It clarifies that the graph ablation uses an inner-product decoder. Appendix B.1 replaces the undifferentiated 44-second ensemble-docking cost with 44 seconds for BRD4(2) and 68 seconds for c-MET, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Guo et al., Zhu and Bento, and Morand et al. for query synthesis, Zhou et al. for molecular optimization, and Dorna et al. for TAGMol. The central positioning against separate generative and surrogate models remains. Numerous other reference edits update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract and contribution edits, explanatory additions, notation corrections and bibliographic language updates. v3 also adds acknowledgments and a conflict-of-interest disclosure and updates correspondence information. The overall narrative and section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram is redrawn and moved from v2 Appendix A, Figure 3, to v3 main-text Figure 2. The mixed-sample results table becomes separate 15- and 40-compound tables. The ablation table and molecule figure are renumbered, and appendix plots are relocated without changing their curves.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by separating the 15- and 40-compound comparisons and specifying statistical-test populations. Added baselines, filtering diagnostics and code-access information modestly strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. The central 40-compound findings remain unchanged. The unexplained revision of the 15-compound MF-LAL values limits confidence in that correction, but the reporting and comparison gains support a limited overall improvement.
